DAISY O. IBANEZ HON. SANTE P. CABRERA Sangguniang Bayan Members Brgy. Binaliw Cebu City Dear SB Members Ibaöez and Cabrera: S. 20 This has reference to your letter dated 11 September 2019, seeking legal opinion from this Department on whether or not the appointment of Punong Barangay Vivian O. Ruste of her brother as a member of Lupong Tagapamayapa constitutes nepotism, and further informing us that the appointment was without a barangay resolution concurring the same. At the outset, Nepotism has been defined by the Civil Service Law as bestowal of patronage by public officers in appointing others to positions by reason of blood or marital relationships to the appointing authorityl. This is prohibited by law and the prohibition has been reiterated in Section 79 of Republic Act No. 7160, or the Local Government Code, viz: "SECTION 79. Limitation on Appointments. - No person shall be appointed in the career service of the local government if he is related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity to the appointing or recommending authority. " Nevertheless, it must be noted that the afore-quoted provision clearly states that it applies only to positions in the career service. Career Service2 is characterized by (I) entrance based on merit and fitness to be determined as far as practicable by competitive examination, or based on highly technical qualifications; (2) opportunity for advancement to higher career positions; and (3) security of tenure. On the other hand, Non-Career Service3 is characterized by (I) entrance on bases other than those of the usual tests of merit and fitness utilized for the career service; and (2) tenure which is limited to a period specified by law, or which is coterminous with that of the appointing authority or subject to 1 DILG Legal opinion No. 18, S.2010 2 Section 7, Chapter 2, Title I, Book V of Executive Order No. 292, or the Administrative Code of 1987 3 Section 8, Chapter 2, Title I, Book V of Executive Order No. 292, or the Administrative Code of 1987

his pleasure, or which is limited to the durations of particular project for which purpose employment was made. Foregoing considered, the Department is of the view that there is no nepotism in the herein case as membership in the Lupong Tagapamayapa is a Non-Career Service position. On the aspect that the appointment was made without your knowledgepnd without Barangay Resolution, your attention is invited to Section 399 of the LGC, which provides: "SECTION. 399. Lupong Tagapamayapa. - (a) There is hereby created in each Barangay a Lupong Tagapamayapa, hereinafter referred to as the lupon, composed of the Punong Barangay as chairman and ten(IO) to twenty (20) members. The lupon shall be constituted every three (3) years in the manner provided herein. (b) Any person actually residing or working in the Barangay, not otherwise expressly disqualified by law, and possessing integrity, impartiality, independence of mind, sense of fairness, and reputation for probity, may be appointed a member of the [upon. (c) A notice to constitute the [upon, which shall include the names of proposed members who have expressed their willingness to serve, shall be prepared by the Punong Barangay within the first fifteen (15) days from the start of his term of office. Such notice shall be posted in three (3) conspicuous places in the Barangay continuously for a period of not less than three(3) weeks; (d) The Punong Barangay, taking into consideration any opposition to the proposed appointment or any recommendations for appointments as may have been made within the period of posting, shall within ten (IO) days thereafter, appoint as members those whom he determines to be suitable therefor. Appointments shall be in writing, signed by the Punong Barangay, and attested to by the Barangay secretary. (e) The list of appointed members shall be posted in three (3) conspicuous places in the Barangay for the entire duration of their term of office; and (f) In Barangays where majority of the inhabitants are members of indigenous cultural communities, local systems of settling disputes through their councils of datus or elders

shall be recognized without prejudice to the applicable provisions of this Code. " The above-quoted provision of the LGC listed the qualifications, as well as the processes in appointing a member of the Lupong Tagapamayapa. The said provision merely requires, aside from the posting requirements, that the appointment shall be in writing signed by the Punong Barangay and attested to by the Barangay Secretary. Thus, a barangay resolution concurring the same is not a requirement. For as long as the above-quoted provision of law has been properly complied and observed, Punong Barangay Ruste did not violate anything, with respect to the appointment of her brother. cc: LS/90 We hope to have addressed your concern sufficiently. Very truly yours, uthority of the Secretary: TIN B. DINO Undersecretary Dir. Leocadio T. Trovela Regional Director DILG-Region VII
